honesty: EVERY NUMBER IN THIS REPORT IS SYNTHETIC-WORLD PERFORMANCE. The dataset is generated by ml/synth.py: bookings, disruptions and outcomes all come from a structural model with latent variables and noise, and the labels are the generator's realized outcomes - not any policy's opinion, and not real freight history. A model scored here has learned the simulated world, nothing more. These numbers say NOTHING about accuracy on real shipments - that would need real TMS history, which sits on the far side of the integration wall - and they must NEVER appear on the product pages (static/), in the README's pitch, or in any demo narration. They exist to compare model families against each other and against the shipped rules engine, inside a world we control end to end.

tabpfn.skipped:
TabPFN is not installed, so the tabpfn backend is skipped. To enable it:
  1. pip install -r ml/requirements.txt   (numpy + scikit-learn)
  2. pip install tabpfn                   (pulls PyTorch - several GB)
  3. run once with network access to huggingface.co - the first fit
     downloads the model weights from Hugging Face, and a sandbox that
     blocks that host (like the one this repo is built in) cannot ever
     run it. That is expected there, not a bug.
License: TabPFN code and v2 weights are Prior-Labs-License (Apache-2.0
plus required 'Built with PriorLabs-TabPFN' attribution when you
distribute); the 2.5/3 weights are NON-COMMERCIAL - internal
benchmarking is fine, shipping is a license decision. tabpfn-client
(their hosted API, no torch) exists but sends the data to Prior Labs'
servers - never point it at real customer bookings without sign-off.
